newsitem.title: CONGO: Mobutu clan cool heels in Congo, seek exile homes.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu clan cool heels in Congo, seek exile homes.

text.p: Fugitive members of ousted President Mobutu Sese Seko's clan cooled their heels in Congo on Sunday after Laurent Kabila's civil war victory in Zaire as their reluctant hosts tried to find countries to take them .
"We're right in the middle of talks with several countries but it's such a delicate business that everything is being kept under wraps," one source at the Congolese presidency said.

Presidency officials said that Congo, anxious to avoid repercussions from its huge neighbour to the south, was keen to see the back of the Mobutu clan -- a group of several dozen people including the veteran strongman's soldier son Kongolo.
"We do want these people to leave Congo as quickly as possible," one Congolese presidential aide told Reuters.
The party included some of those who profited most from Mobutu's three decades rule over Africa's third largest and one of its potentially richest countries.
As they waited at Brazzaville's Maya-Maya airport a rebel spokesman in France said Mobutu and his clan would be pursued.

"With us, he will never be in peace. Wherever he goes, we will find him," Zamba Afri Kounyen told radio France-Info. "We regard them as criminals who must be detained and taken to trial by a people's court," he said.

The Congolese presidential aide said the group, among them General Nzimbi Ngbale, commander of Mobutu's once-feared presidential guard, had planned to leave on Saturday on Mobutu's presidential jet but the crew had refused to take them.
The plane eventually left for Gabon but had not been allowed to stay there and had returned to Congo's capital Brazzaville, the aide added. It was not clear who piloted the plane.
The initial plan, the aide said, had been to fly from Gabon to Mobutu's jungle palace at his ancestral home in Gbadolite, northern Zaire, and from there on to Morocco.

An official in Rabat told Reuters earlier that Mobutu was already in Morocco at a luxury hotel south of the capital. A friend of Mobutu's family said he had spoken with Gbadolite on Sunday and Mobutu was still there.
The Congolese presidential aide said the party was now divided on its next move.

Younger members were reluctant to go by charter to Gbadolite, now that rebels had control of most of their country. Older members argued that they had valid visas to various countries and could fly on with regular commercial flights.
Witnesses said about 40 members of the party later left the airport by bus and taxi but some family members stayed behind.
Mobutu, fighting cancer, slipped out of Kinshasa quietly on Friday and travelled to Gbadolite. Kabila's forces moved into Kinshasa on Saturday.
Mobutu, 66, seized power in 1965 and proved one of the continent's most enduring strongmen. Western powers supported him as a Cold War bastion against Soviet communism.
Denounced as everything from a dictator to a thief, critics say he plundered Zaire and amassed a huge personal fortune while his people struggled against poverty and neglect.
As the Mobutu clan waited at the airport, Kabila's rebels moved to consolidate their hold over Kinshasa -- just five km (three miles) across the river from Brazzaville.
Kongolo, an officer in the presidential guard, fled Kinshasa on Saturday in a speed boat with 20 other men.
Nzimbi, who fled on Friday, commanded the Special Presidential Division (DSP), which ensured Mobutu's personal security. Most of the force came from Mobutu's Ngbandi tribe.
